TRIAGE DIRECTIVE (operator ruling 2026-10-03): this is an IMPLEMENTATION CHORE. Its specification and design are settled and accepted: openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/ (merged as 7f0aa4ad, council-cleared in run build-decision-0065-slice-two-co-50ef1e34) and decision 0077 (accepted). Do not re-specify or re-design: classify it `chore` so it goes straight to implement. It is still reviewed by the full engine council. If the settled design cannot be implemented as written, the implement seat reports blocked; triage does not reopen the design.

BUILD DECISION 0065, SLICE TWO — UNIT U8a2c, one narrow visit, ONE pull request. Branch s2/U8a2c, cut from main at db59dfe1. Recipe claude-flash-dsh-adv.

READ FIRST: design.md's "Slice two units" preamble and your unit (below, verbatim), the tasks your unit closes in tasks.md, the spec deltas it names, operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md, decision 0077 and decision 0065. Units before yours in your row's Dependencies have landed on main.

THE PREAMBLE, verbatim:
## Slice two units

One row is one PR, from main, signed and through the merge queue after the
operator rules. Follow this order. Dependencies are semantic prerequisites,
not simply the preceding row; the independence of U1–U4 is explicit in D9.
No row through U9a lifts the MCP compile fence. U9b is the sole enabling PR.
The lettered splits are required by the checked seams: record schema plus
embedded copy already consumes two files; multi-server wiring crosses runtime,
protocol and adapter data; storage/folding/inspect crosses CLI, protocol,
runtime and pure view. Minimal ledger writing is deliberately pulled into U6.

`contracts/realms.v<N>.schema.json` denotes one exact future file allocated
as **the next realms version after v7** at U5c, including v7's fields. It is
the only intentionally deferred filename number. Every other production path
below is literal. New paths are proposed modules/schemas, not files created
by this document plan. Constructors/registration are counted in their row.
Future tests extend the named suites; capability_broker already exists under
the consolidated CLI integration binary. New capability_artifacts and runtime
capability_ledger/capability_broker_launch modules are registered through the
existing test-only roots (CLI tests/it.rs and runtime tests/it.rs), not new
undeclared binaries. Tests may use child modules of the owning suites to stay
below 2,000 lines; list every test move in unit evidence.

Each row closes exactly its numbered tasks, including tests/mutations and
gate evidence. Test lists below are the allowed owning suites; every row
also updates this change's tasks and later implementation evidence. Measured
witness/compose pins accompany only rows that change their inputs.

YOUR ROW, verbatim:
| U8a2c | U8a2a | Build every workspace box from the reach sealed at admission; 38.3–38.4 | `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/hands.rs`; `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/native_controls/mcp.rs`; `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/mcp.rs`; `crates/brokkr-cli/src/hands.rs`; `crates/brokkr-cli/src/lib.rs`; `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/probe/observe.rs`; `crates/brokkr-cli/src/doctor.rs`; `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs`; `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/broker.rs` |

YOUR UNIT, verbatim:
### U8a2c — Build every workspace box from the reach sealed at admission

Carry each writer's reach, as U8a2a sealed it in the writer's reservation, to hands, and build every box of that writer from it, so nothing a writer changes inside its reach after admission changes what a later box mounts. The sealed reach is every bind source and the worktree's Git directory and common directory, each by canonical path and device/inode. Hands takes each bind's source from its sealed canonical path rather than resolving the authored spelling again, and takes the Git directories from the sealed reach instead of asking Git for them at each call. Before each box starts, and again once its argv is final (as U8a's confirm does), it observes each sealed source and the worktree's Git pointer again; a source, ancestor or pointer that no longer resolves to its sealed identity refuses with MB3's identity cause before spawn. An unchanged writer's repeated calls run as before. No new authored HandsSpec key. Admission's exclusion (D6) is unchanged, and this does not replace it.

The engine carries the sealed reach as U8a carries the artifact root: `Transport` gains it (checked field by field where a transport is compared), the hands serve and exec arguments carry it, and every engine `Transport` constructor passes it. The adapter probe and doctor's box probe, which admit nothing, seal their own reach the same way when they start. No path builds a box from unsealed reach: a missing or unreadable sealed reach refuses, never falls back to deriving it again.

Closes tasks 38.3 and 38.4 with U8a2a and U8a2b (operator ruling 2026-10-18); requirements [CR2](specs/capability-response-retention/spec.md), [MB3](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md).
Proof: In real namespaces, after admission a writer's own box replaces a bind source beneath its worktree, or an ancestor of one, by a symlink, rename or hardlink toward protected evidence or the coordination root, and separately rewrites the worktree's Git pointer or its per-worktree `commondir` to name another repository's Git directory. Its next workspace call and a following exec each refuse before spawn with MB3's exact cause, the protected bytes and the other repository unchanged, while an unchanged writer's repeated calls, legitimate worktree writes and commits run. Independently remove the sealed carriage (hands derives its reach again) and the drift check, each failing its own test.

Operator ruling 2026-10-18, splitting this unit from U8a2a after U8a2a's third run held (0065-slice-two-unit-u8a2a-see-th-88d31f37, REVIEW-SECURITY-HOLD): protocol hands rebuilt each workspace box from what it read again at every call, so an admitted writer could redirect a later box of its own after the dispatch door's recheck, and refusing every writer able to do so would refuse every run in a linked Git worktree once U9b1 lifts the fence. The remedy belongs in hands, so it is its own unit, landing after U8a2a and before U8a2b and U9b1. Its row names the files U8a's carriage of the artifact root needed, with engine/broker.rs, where the reservation holds the sealed reach. Files frozen at their baselines (hands.rs, lib.rs, doctor.rs, engine.rs) grow only through new private child modules under the standing rule. The public API rise this needs is approved as measured, up to +10 lines across quality/public-api/brokkr-protocol.txt, brokkr-runtime.txt and brokkr-cli.txt together; a larger rise comes back to the operator.

Operator ruling 2026-10-18, after U8a2a's fourth run parked (0065-slice-two-unit-u8a2a-see-th-3a0cc19c): this unit also fixes the three medium residuals accepted as debt on U8a2a, in the modules U8a2a added beneath engine/broker/ (root.rs and historical.rs) with their tests. R1: no reseal reports failure or lateness while only its successor stands; it either reports failure with the record that stood still named, its bytes and identity unchanged, or reports itself committed, a failure after that point failing the run under the fence rule; the deadline is observed at every step up to the commit. R2: historical hashing is incremental and observes the shared deadline as it hashes. R3: the link-failure proof refuses the link alone while the rename stays possible. R1's proof drives that last step for join, unresolved-cleanup marking, release and recovery; each fix has an independent compiling control that fails its own test.

Owning tests: `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/hands/tests.rs`, `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/boundary_tests.rs`.

CONTROLLER'S STATE FOR THIS RUN (the-forge-67, 2026-10-18). This is U8a2c's FIRST RUN.
- The operator split U8a2c from U8a2a on 2026-10-18, after U8a2a's third run held. The ruling is in design.md: U8a2c's section, U8a2a's second ruling paragraph, and D6's new last coordination sentence. Read all three.
- U8a2a has landed on main. Its reservation holds each writer's sealed reach (every bind source and both Git directories, by canonical path and device/inode), and its dispatch door rechecks that reach before spawn. Build on what U8a2a sealed; don't build a second sealing of your own.

OPERATOR RULINGS (design.md, U8a2c section; the PR carries them): the row's files, and a public API rise of at most +10 lines across quality/public-api/brokkr-protocol.txt, brokkr-runtime.txt and brokkr-cli.txt together. Record the measured rise in evidence. Anything larger comes back to the operator at PR time.

The reviewer's findings, for reference:
  - R1: root.rs's reseal unlinks the record that stood and then syncs the directory; a sync failure there returns Unsealed with only the successor named, and that step never checks expiry.
  - R2: historical.rs collects up to 8 MiB plus one and hashes the buffer once after its last budget check.
  - R3: admission/tests/sealing.rs's Late::Deny removes directory write permission, refusing both linkat and the rename after it, so changing the non-NOENT link error arm still passes.

CONTROLLER NOTES (the controller's own, not the operator's):
- U8a (#729) is the closest precedent: it carried the artifact root to hands as a typed `Transport` fact and as the hands serve and exec arguments. That needed every file in this row except engine/broker.rs: clap's `HandsCommand` in brokkr-cli/src/lib.rs, cli/src/hands.rs, the adapter probe in probe/observe.rs, and doctor's box probe in doctor.rs. Its tests are in protocol hands/tests.rs and runtime engine/boundary_tests.rs.
- hands.rs, lib.rs, doctor.rs and engine.rs are frozen at their baselines. New code goes in new private children under the standing rule.
- Real-box tests (bwrap) take the HANDS_BOX_ENV skip in your seat. Name each one in evidence as "host result pending". Before merge the controller runs them on the host, along with exact coverage.
- No test may resolve the real HOME's coordination root, or write the test process's own environment outside the house EnvGuard. U8a2a's runs leaked reservations into the operator's HOME three times.
- If your change moves any witness digest (crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/witnesses.json), re-bless it and list the moved rows in evidence. A concurrent change re-pins bundle rows there.
- The `KNOWN OPEN` comment in box_argv (the common directory bound read-write) is decision 0054's open item, not this unit's. Leave it as it stands.
- From U7c's and U7d2's CI failures:
  - macOS runs every test on APFS, which refuses non-UTF-8 names. Such fixtures go behind cfg(target_os = "linux"), with a comment saying why.
  - Imports used only by Linux code are cfg-gated too.
  - The exact coverage gate counts every closure as a function, and every `if` condition and match guard as a branch. Reach every new refusal from a test.
- U8a2a's reviewer noted (INFO, not ruled) that ordinary admission tests still read the host's /proc/self/mountinfo through exclusion::shown_once, and failed in one review environment. If a test you add or touch depends on that, inject the mount observation instead.
- U8a2a's host check (2026-10-18), not ruled: under a group-writable TMPDIR, tests/capability_broker_launch.rs's HOME-resolution proof makes its HOME under TMPDIR (support/own_home.rs uses tempfile::tempdir) and skips with 'no protected location'. If you touch support/own_home.rs or that test, place the HOME in a protected location as Host::resolving does (TMPDIR, else /tmp, else /var/tmp). Otherwise record it; don't block on it.

STANDING RULINGS. Decision 0065's hold: off by default, no grandfathering; realm-only grants; tools are an abstraction, dialects the concrete; refuse, never reconcile (slice one's operator ruling of 2026-09-23). The MCP compile fence stays in place until U9b. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063). Main's code-health rules bind: no `unsafe` in brokkr-runtime; `#[expect(.., reason)]`, never `#[allow]`; clippy's too_many_lines, excessive_nesting and struct_excessive_bools are denied, so split, and only if splitting would widen your unit carry `reason = "baseline 2026-09-29, decision 0065 slice one merged with main; split after #319"`; when a count moves, re-measure quality/'s file-lines, too-many-lines and suppressions (the steps quality/measure.sh uses), witness pins with `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test witness_digests` (or, once #423's single test binary is on your base — crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/it.rs exists — `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it witness_digests::`), and budgets with scripts/measure-budgets.sh. Where a crate has tests/it.rs, a NEW tests/*.rs file must be registered as `mod <file>;` in that crate's tests/it.rs (layering::test_targets refuses an unregistered one), unless it sets HOME, cwd, env or a global allocator, in which case it is its own [[test]] in Cargo.toml with the reason written there; and `--test <file>` filters become `--test it <file>::` (capability_launch stays its own binary).

RULES. Touch at most the production files your row names; if the real scope exceeds them, STOP and report `oversized` with the split. One exception, the operator's standing rule of 2026-10-09 (operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md): beside a production file in your row that sits at its 800-line ceiling, or is frozen at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline above it, you may add NEW private child modules, declared from that file, in its own module tree and consumed in this unit, without stopping. The same holds beside a row file that your own change would push past 800 lines (extended 2026-10-11). You may also change an EXISTING private child module of a file in your row, in that file's own module tree (extended 2026-10-11). You may move existing code out of the full file into such a child to make room, preferring the code your change touches. Name each new file in your evidence and commit, and set its quality/file-lines.txt row. You may also add a name to an EXISTING re-export in the parent module that declares one of your row's files, where the parent's line count does not change (extended 2026-10-10). Files in any other module tree still mean `oversized`; any public API growth still needs the operator's ruling at PR time (record it, do not stop). Test files are NOT bounded by the row (controller's standing clarification, 2026-10-05): a test anywhere that pins behaviour your unit changes, a validator or fixture swap in another suite, or a new child test module beside an owning suite that sits over its line ceiling is part of your unit — size-neutral wherever a file sits at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline. A LOW finding you cannot fix inside your row's production files: record it in your result and do NOT report blocked for it. Tests assert exact reasons and values, never is_err(); every new test is bound by a compiling mutation that makes it fail, then restored, recorded (test, assertion) in evidence.md. Tick a task in tasks.md only on observed evidence; record results in a NEW file of your own, openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/evidence/U8a2c.md (two lanes deliver units at once, and every unit appending to evidence.md made each pair of pull requests conflict), and do not edit evidence.md itself; write it in prose or a table — never as a bullet list of the standard gate lines (`cargo fmt ...: clean`, `cargo clippy ...: clean`), which earlier evidence files already hold word for word, so the data clone gate refuses it; never edit the tasks.md preamble. Fixtures build on a canonicalised temporary root; no test reads .forge/ or needs an installed provider. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/ and extensions/ do not move unless your unit names them. Sign every commit (`git commit -S`; main requires signatures). HEADLESS SEAT: your session ends the moment you end a turn — never run a command in the background, never use Monitor or ScheduleWakeup, run every command in the foreground under the tool's 10-minute limit (suites crate by crate with `timeout 590`, split by --lib/--test if longer), and write your result file before you finish. GATES: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; the suite of each crate you touched; openspec validate --all --strict; typos --hidden; git diff --check; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones. CI also builds and tests on macOS, which this host cannot: Linux-only code (namespaces, mountinfo, /proc, device numbers, Linux-only syscalls) goes behind `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` with a non-Linux stand-in that refuses, as broker/session.rs does, and any libc or rustix type you use must be the same type on both (rustix's Dev is u64 on Linux and i32 on macOS; U6c6a's first PR failed to compile there). Keep the session small; commit when the unit is done; never push.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.
instructions.review:

Create or adopt `openspec/changes/<change>/proposal.md`, then write the capability deltas under `specs/`. The proposal keeps `Why`, `What Changes`, and `Capabilities`; each delta uses requirements and scenarios. On return, answer every finding in the artifacts and keep the proposal and deltas coherent.

# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.
